pages.text: Air for your EVA suit once the atmosphere freezes.

pages.title: Use
pages.text: Carry one while wearing the full $(l:orsa_equipment/eva_suit)EVA suit$(/l). It draws automatically: $(bold)10 units$() per second of breathing.$(br2)$(flavor)Hyperventilating does not conserve oxygen. We checked.$()

pages.title: Tanks
pages.text: $(bold)Mk.I$(): 120 s, cyan bar$(br)$(bold)Mk.II$(): 240 s, blue bar$(br)$(bold)Mk.III$(): 360 s, purple bar$(br2)Tanks drain one at a time. The HUD shows the total.

pages.title: Refilling
pages.text: Put a canister in a $(l:advanced/geothermal_core)Geothermal Core$(/l) O2 slot. Bigger tanks take longer.$(br2)The Core refills from spare oxygen only; rooms come first.
Canisters, reservoirs, intact EVA suits and airlock reserves share the spare.$(br2)An intact suit also tops up carried canisters while you stand in supported breathable air.

pages.title: O2 Canister Mk.I
pages.text: Iron, glass and a Thermal Core.$(br2)$(flavor)ORSA assumed you'd have airlocks. Kevin spent the airlock budget on an espresso machine.$()

pages.title: O2 Canister Mk.II
pages.text: Diamonds around the first canister. Enough air to leave shelter, finish a job and get back.$(br2)$(flavor)The priciest air you'll ever breathe, until the Mk.III.$()

pages.title: O2 Canister Mk.III
pages.text: $(l:advanced/frozen_atmosphere_shard)Atmosphere Shards$(/l), blue ice and a Mk.II.$(br2)$(flavor)You are bottling the sky.$()
